note: The desktop-app capture, run on Antigravity 2.19.1 (the desktop app), macOS 27.0 arm64, 2026-10-04, with ACC 0.8.5 installed. The operator opened a project in the app and sent one prompt; ACC's installed hooks attached the conversation. A separate process read the language server's command line, took the CSRF token only into one child's environment, found the HTTP port in the server's log, and ran agy agentapi send-message once into the idle conversation, rendered as ACC's relay renders a peer message. Nothing printed or recorded holds the token. The conversation id is real; the probe project path is redacted.

findings: the desktop app runs ACC's global hooks under its language server, with no agy in the process tree
an idle desktop conversation woke within a second of an agentapi push with the language server's own token and HTTP port, and the model answered with acc reply

the agent's commands run in a sandbox where ACC's wrapper cannot run; the model retries outside it after the app's approval, and the app keeps that grant in config.json, not in Antigravity CLI's settings
the token and the HTTP port are readable from outside the app: the token on the language server's command line, the port in its log and from lsof
